name: PDPPL
title: Qatar Personal Data Privacy Protection Law (Law No. 13 of 2016)
notice: Plain-language summaries written for Assayr to help track obligations. They are guidance, not legal advice, and not the text of the law: check every obligation against the official text and your legal adviser.

obligations.title: Process personal data fairly and lawfully
obligations.summary: Handle personal data honestly and only in ways the law allows, for purposes people would reasonably expect.

obligations.title: Use data only for the stated purpose
obligations.summary: Collect personal data for specific, explicit purposes and do not reuse it for unrelated ones without a new basis.

obligations.title: Collect no more than needed
obligations.summary: Keep the personal data you collect to what is necessary for the purpose.

obligations.title: Keep data accurate
obligations.summary: Take reasonable steps to keep personal data accurate and up to date, and correct it when asked.

obligations.title: Keep data no longer than necessary
obligations.summary: Set a retention period for each use of personal data, review it, and securely delete or anonymise data that is no longer needed.

obligations.title: Have a lawful basis for each processing
obligations.summary: Record why each processing activity is allowed, such as consent, a contract, a legal duty or a legitimate interest.

obligations.title: Obtain and record valid consent
obligations.summary: Where consent is the basis, get it clearly before processing, keep a record of how it was given, and make withdrawal easy.

obligations.title: Tell people how their data is used
obligations.summary: Give individuals clear information about who you are, what data you process, why, who receives it and how to exercise their rights.

obligations.title: Let people access their data
obligations.summary: Have a process to confirm whether you hold someone's data and give them a copy within the required time.

obligations.title: Correct, erase or restrict on request
obligations.summary: Handle requests to correct, delete, restrict or object to processing, and record the outcome and reasons for any refusal.

obligations.title: Respond within the deadline
obligations.summary: Track every request against its due date so none is answered late.

obligations.title: Protect personal data with suitable measures
obligations.summary: Apply technical and organisational security measures that match the risk, such as access control, encryption and logging.

obligations.title: Limit who can see personal data
obligations.summary: Give access to personal data only to people who need it for their role, and review that access.

obligations.title: Prevent data leakage
obligations.summary: Use controls that stop personal data leaving the organisation without authorisation, including on devices and in transfers.

obligations.title: Train staff on handling personal data
obligations.summary: Make sure staff who handle personal data know their responsibilities through awareness training.

obligations.title: Detect and record personal data breaches
obligations.summary: Keep a register of breaches affecting personal data with what happened, who is affected and what was done.

obligations.title: Notify the authority and people affected in time
obligations.summary: When a breach may cause serious harm, tell the competent authority and the people affected without undue delay and within the deadline you track.

obligations.title: Learn from breaches
obligations.summary: Review each breach and record lessons learnt to stop it happening again.

obligations.title: Extra care for sensitive data
obligations.summary: Treat health, biometric, religious, criminal, ethnic and similar data as sensitive, and assess the risk before processing it.

obligations.title: Assess high-risk processing
obligations.summary: Carry out and approve a privacy impact assessment for processing that is likely to be high risk.

obligations.title: Protect children's data
obligations.summary: Apply additional safeguards and parental involvement where you process children's personal data.

obligations.title: Control transfers outside Qatar
obligations.summary: Know which processing sends data outside Qatar, to which countries, and that the transfer is allowed and protected.

obligations.title: Marketing only with permission
obligations.summary: Send electronic direct marketing only with prior consent, identify yourself, and offer an easy way to opt out.

obligations.title: Choose processors that protect data
obligations.summary: Check the security of processors and vendors before they handle personal data and review them regularly.

obligations.title: Bind processors by agreement
obligations.summary: Have a written agreement with every processor that sets out what they may do with the data and how they protect it.

obligations.title: Keep a record of processing
obligations.summary: Maintain an up-to-date record of processing activities, the data involved and where it is kept.

obligations.title: Know where personal data is stored
obligations.summary: Keep an inventory of the systems and assets that hold personal data.

obligations.title: Be able to show compliance
obligations.summary: Keep evidence, reviews and approvals that demonstrate how you meet your privacy obligations.

obligations.title: Assign privacy responsibility
obligations.summary: Name a person or team responsible for personal data protection with the authority to act.

obligations.title: Have an approved privacy policy
obligations.summary: Approve and publish a policy on personal data protection and review it regularly.
